differences.text: Starts collapsed unless `open` is written (like `<details>`). Upstream defaultIsOpen defaults to true; a boolean attribute cannot default to true and be turned off from HTML, and the inverted name the mapping rules prescribe (`collapsed`) would make `open` a second name for the same state. Banner, which upstream starts collapsed, matches. Write `open` on items that must start open.

Collapsed content uses hidden="until-found" where supported, so browser find in page reveals and opens the item (beforematch syncs the state); elsewhere it is plainly hidden. Upstream uses display: none, which is invisible to find in page. The reveal cannot be vetoed, so only tct-after-open-change fires for it.

The stylesheet does not use the shared base: base's `[hidden] { display: none !important }` (reset layer) cannot be overridden and would defeat hidden="until-found". The rest of base is repeated in the component's reset layer. See requests.

Inside a group the item fires no tct-open-change; the group fires the cancelable tct-value-change with the requested selection. Row chrome (dividers, density, chevron position) reaches only the group's direct items: a collapsible nested in another one re-provides the group state without the chrome.

requests.reason: The NewExpression check /^Tct[A-Z]/ also flags event classes (`new TctOpenChangeEvent(...)`, `new TctValueChangeEvent(...)`), which every intent-event owner must construct. Exclude names ending in `Event`; until then the files that construct events carry a file-level eslint-disable naming this reason.

Let components use hidden="until-found": exclude it from the important display:none rule, then tct-collapsible (and later tab panels, accordions in other families) can adopt base again and drop their reset copy.

core.collapsible.notes: Guides: [mwg:search-hidden-content] (hidden=until-found, beforematch state sync, fallback to plain hidden) [mwg:accessible-web-components] (trigger and region in one shadow root, aria-controls stays valid) [mwg:animate-to-intrinsic-sizes] (considered; upstream does not animate the height, neither do we).

api.notes: Attribute `value`: the initial open item(s), space separated for `multiple`.
Current open item(s): string for single ('' when none), string[] for multiple.
Cancelable intent event before a user toggle; `value` is the requested selection in the same shape as the property.

differences.text: Upstream is uncontrolled or controlled through value/onChange; here the group owns its selection like a native control (D-006): a user toggle fires tct-value-change first and applies unless prevented; a controlled framework sets `value` back. Property and attribute writes fire nothing.

A group without dividers adds no box (display: contents), like upstream's DOM-less group; with has-dividers it is a flex column and each item draws its own hairline (first item exempt through :host(:first-child)).
